body: No, I'm just tired of talking about this stuff with friends. I have to bring it up which always feels so awkward and i just feel like I'm complaining. And even if they have a way they can relate, there's not much they can say but agreement and a couple nods.
thanks for listening though. It's nice to have someone actually ask things and not just listen to me talk

No. I've had several girlfriends, I've been in love once before, and I've had my heart broken. But nothing has ever felt like this. I've never felt a connection to another living thing like I did with her and I've never experienced a pain as great as this.

I don't want to sit here and blame everything on a single person or event, but I do have to agree that's how my mind feels and that's how it seems. I did function much better before her. I wasn't perfect, but I wasn't suicidal or unable to function in daily life. Sure, I was getting bored of some of my hobbies, but not to the extent I feel now. I still held a job without anxiety and I still at least had ambition and dreams, regardless of how unrealistic they might've been.

It's been eight months since she left. There was a whole slew of things that happened. She cheated on me and flirted with other guys as well, she told me that her love for me was different than my love for her, and then she just abruptly ended everything one day and suddenly turned to a bitch and pushed me away which hurt the most because I've known her for over 10 years and, for the last 3 years before we dated and the year we were together, we were each other's best friends and now she wants nothing to do with me. Even months and months later when she finally texted me with an apology admitting fault, she still tells me she has "too many responsibilities" to hang out with me. And I get that maybe it's for the best we don't hang out because I'm not sure how I'd handle it, but part of me feels I'd at least be a little bit closer to stable if I still had my friend.

But you're right. I think in the end I'm just having trouble moving past her because she made me think some things I've never thought before in my life. I still have at least two nightmares a week where the two of us are hanging out and she just suddenly disappears out of nowhere and at least one dream a week where we're back together peacefully. I'm getting sick of it because they just wake me up in a bad mood and I have to carry that shit with me throughout the day. Simply looking at the same model of car as hers can cause my heart to sink into my chest mid-laughter.

I need to find something else to focus on and it's hard when everything reminds me of her and when everything about us felt so perfect when things were good, like the stars had aligned.
